result.title: Decoding the Functional Roles of Register and High-Norm Patch Tokens in Vision Transformers
result.summary: Self-supervised Vision Transformers (ViTs), such as DINOv2, learn rich visual representations, but the functions of their internal tokens remain poorly understood. Recent architectures introduce dedicated register tokens to reduce high-norm out- lier patch tokens that emerge in background re- gions, yet the semantic and functional roles of both token types have not been fully established. In this paper, we analyze these roles by training sparse autoencoders (SAEs) on register-token and outlier-token activations in DINOv2. Using an automated interpretability pipeline, UMAP clus- tering, and CLIP-space cross-checks, we find that register-token features are more strongly associ- ated with high-level semantic concepts. Outlier- token features, by contrast, are more often associ- ated with lower-level structural, background, and texture-dominant patterns. Causal ablations fur- ther reveal a substantial functional asymmetry: disrupting top-activating register-derived features produces a 48.17% drop in representation cosine similarity, whereas disrupting outlier-derived fea- tures produces only a 0.31% drop. Together, our results provide evidence for token specialization in self-supervised ViTs.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文用稀疏自编码器分析 DINOv2 中 register token 与高范数离群 patch token，结合自动可解释性、UMAP 聚类和 CLIP 空间交叉验证，并做因果消融，发现两类 token 存在功能不对称：register 特征偏高层语义，离群 patch 特征偏背景与纹理结构。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非 VLM 推理工作，但其对内部 token 功能分工与因果消融的刻画，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据如何保留在内部状态、哪些状态携带任务必要信息提供可核查的分析线索。
